summary: The ancient damping chamber is held at an isolated preparatory charge while technicians reconcile a network that has expanded far beyond its original calibration.
settingText: Full-page image inside the damping chamber: monumental emitters, layered old engineering, and tiny human figures working beneath machinery built for a more cautious age. Through apertures and instrument light, the still-vast High Era corridor network remains active above.
panelPlan: One full-page opening editorial image: old damping emitters sustained in a quiet local precharge under later retrofit cabling, with huge dormant network couplings dominating the space.
Convey potential power, historical age, and the danger of the unfinished matrix without showing a network-wide damping pulse, catastrophe, or invented readable lettering.
directionInline: No captions, speech balloons, or readable environmental labels. High Era historical design only.
Continue directly from Issue 2 page 23: Iskara ordered local preparation despite Council denial; the chamber remains isolated and no network pulse has yet fired.

summary: Working through the chamber's precharge, Liora and Alan discover that later network extensions were fed through an old distribution bus never intended for the present system load.
panelPlan: Re-establish the same chamber in local precharge from Issue 2's final scene; Liora and Alan are already working there, not entering or discovering it again.
Alan traces an old emitter bus through several visibly newer branching retrofits and compares their combined load with the original Dawn Era distribution scheme.
Liora tests the load map against the incomplete historical calibration: the old design appears sound for its original reach, not for every later attachment.
Finish on the modern branches converging at an underspecified old control point, revealing a new limitation rather than repeating the first discovery of half-percent phase shear.
directionInline: Preserve exact chamber geometry and accumulated state from Issue 2. No renewed first-entry or discovery staging.
Independent calibration work is ongoing. Local precharge is not a live network damping cycle.

dialogueInline.text: Precharge is steady. Look where the new branches terminate.
They're all feeding the old bus.
The drawing only accounts for the original load.
Before we pulse anything, map every added branch.

summary: With the new branch mapping assembled, Alan discovers that the modern remote-control layer can alter local emitter trims during an otherwise carefully calibrated damping cycle.
panelPlan: Alan builds a network-coupled simulation using the now mapped modern branches, explicitly contrasting it with the original Dawn Era control geometry.
Simulation insert: the old design's trim remains under local command, but the modern retrofit controller accepts changes along an independent remote-write path.
Liora traces the path from BHA remote maintenance into the chamber's local matrix; even correct initial phase calibration could be overwritten mid-cycle.
End on Liora choosing to isolate ordinary remote writes before the first live pulse, a new operational safeguard rather than another demonstration of the mismatch already seen in Issue 2.
directionInline: Do not repeat Issue 2 page 22's half-percent shear demonstration as a new discovery.
Use physical engineering signals and consistent controller topology; never imply magical field manipulation.

dialogueInline.text: The original circuit holds in the model.
It can still write to local trim.
Any time the remote path is open.
Cut ordinary remote write before we begin.

summary: Liora disables the ordinary remote-write channel and tells Alan to alarm on the surviving chair-level emergency-maintenance path, protecting local control without knowing Lochran will later exploit the exception.
panelPlan: Liora and Alan isolate the modern remote-control link from the damping controller while the local precharge and calibration work remain uninterrupted.
Alan checks the cutover: the ordinary remote command route is inactive, but a separately wired emergency-maintenance path remains available to BHA chair-level authority.
Liora explicitly instructs Alan to flag any activation of that exceptional path; they treat it as a material unresolved risk, not a harmless status field.
Close with the two control routes visually distinct: local calibration protected against normal access, emergency chair-level write authority still dormant and monitorable.
directionInline: Do not show an unscripted readable 'LOCAL CONTROL' label; use physical isolation, separate conduits and status lighting.
This establishes the exact mechanism later used in Issue 3 pages 12–15; Iskara's Issue 2 preparation order did not authorize this separate chair-level write path.

dialogueInline.text: Yes. There's a separate emergency-maintenance path.
Flag it. If that path wakes up, I need the alarm before the matrix changes.

summary: After learning that Iskara proceeded with local preparation, Lochran decides the unauthorized damping effort must also yield visible stability for a public already losing confidence.
panelPlan: Inside the BHA Nexus, Damian informs Lochran that Iskara authorized a local precharge after the Council refused the restriction plan.
Lochran views worsening public transport status beside confirmation that the damping chamber has not yet fired a live network cycle.
He asks whether apparently chaotic public stability metrics will persist even if the engineers begin relieving actual load.
Damian demonstrates that public-facing readout smoothing would pass through operational coefficients, not a harmless communication filter; Lochran demands the proposed package.
directionInline: Lochran knows the chamber preparation is unauthorized but chooses to shape its public consequences rather than immediately halt it.
Distinguish communication intent from engineering control; do not show him unaware of the interface between the two.

dialogueInline.text: Iskara ordered precharge. The network connection is still isolated.
After the Council denied the reduction?
She put her name on it.
If they recover the field and the public boards still show collapse, what happens at the ports?
You want the stability readouts smoothed.
I want to see what that would require.

summary: Damian learns the proposed stability coefficients conflict with the engineers' active calibration and knowingly prepares the public explanation for a chair-authorized override.
panelPlan: Damian compares the proposed coefficient package with the active chamber matrix and the engineers' blocked-deployment warning.
Lochran notes the political danger of a public-facing recovery that looks like increasing instability; Damian makes the engineering contradiction explicit.
Lochran chooses chair-level deployment despite the lack of engineering sign-off and accepts formal responsibility.
Damian drafts contingency language minimizing expected objections, but his hesitation shows that he now knows a political decision may directly alter the machinery.

dialogueInline.text: Engineering marked these coefficients do not deploy.
Under this one. They don't match Liora's matrix.
The public cannot navigate on contradictory stability figures.
If we deploy them, the chamber could get contradictory commands.
Prepare the override. I'll authorize it.
Then I'll have to explain why we ignored the warning.

directionInline: Damian is complicit, not oblivious. The shift from messaging to field control is explicit.
The package is prepared here; its later dispatch and chair-key activation occur in Issue 3 pages 12–13, not early.
No invented readable console phrases; safety flags can be displayed graphically.

summary: In the Outer Band, Ruben watches a critical node vibrate out of pattern while the damping attempt is being prepared elsewhere.
panelPlan: Wide outer-ring engineering space with warning stripes flickering and a deep structural shudder traveling through the floor.
Ruben places a hand on a support and feels the vibration before the instruments catch it.
A beacon log shows the node slipping out of the expected harmonic rhythm.
End on a fastener or brace visibly working loose under the repeated pulse.
directionInline: Keep the physical danger immediate and tactile.

dialogueInline.text: Put your hand here. The vibration's in the metal, not the mount.

summary: The outer technician warns that if the damping chamber fails, neglected peripheral stations will absorb the first catastrophic consequences.
panelPlan: The technician marks the Outer Band’s position on a network load map.
Failure propagation reaches the outer stations before the protected central routes.
Ruben compares the projection to the hardware already shaking around them.
End on the technician demanding that the Core understand who is carrying the first risk.
directionInline: Establish that peripheral stations carry the first and greatest exposure if the intervention fails.

dialogueInline.text: Send it anyway. Maybe somebody looks at the part marked 'Outer first.'

summary: Liora begins the first live network-connected damping pulse after completing chamber-local precharge and isolating ordinary remote write; old emitters answer unevenly before approaching a fragile alignment.
panelPlan: Visually connect the previously isolated chamber to the network for the first time, distinct from the chamber-local diagnostic and precharge of Issue 2.
Power enters the live damping cycle in measured stages; old emitters flare at slightly different moments.
Liora and Alan correct local phase differences as the floor shivers hard enough to force them to brace.
Finish on the first tentative convergence of the network-wide pulse, with the separately monitored emergency chair-level write path still dormant.
directionInline: This is the first live network damping cycle, not a repetition of the preparatory precharge shown at the end of Issue 2.
Keep the remote-access hazard visually consistent with Issue 3 pages 3–4 and the later political override.

dialogueInline.text: I see it. Hold the secondaries.

summary: For the first time in cycles, the harmonic field visibly stabilizes and corridor stress starts to ease.
panelPlan: Wide chamber panel: after several uneven pulses, the emitter rings finally begin answering one another instead of fighting.
Two-shot on Liora and Alan watching the stress curve bend for the first time in cycles; neither leaves the controls.
Final quiet close on the improving field trace as Alan almost celebrates and Liora refuses to tempt it.
directionInline: Allow a real moment of earned hope.

dialogueInline.text: Hold the secondaries at current power.

summary: Alan confirms two-percent drift—the best reading they have seen in cycles—while both know the margin remains dangerously small.
panelPlan: Alan checks independent instruments to confirm the improvement is real.
The two-percent figure holds across more than one sensor.
Liora keeps her hands on the controls instead of celebrating.
End on the stabilized field surrounded by amber warning limits.
directionInline: Keep the improvement visibly real but fragile, surrounded by narrow safety margins and warning limits.

summary: A Coalition technician receives Lochran's chair-level emergency command, which reopens the local lockout and presents stability coefficients that contradict the active calibration.
panelPlan: At the BHA Nexus, the Coalition technician sees an emergency-maintenance authorization signed with Lochran's chair credential reopen a channel marked locally locked.
The technician compares the incoming stability coefficients to the live chamber matrix and gets an immediate validation conflict.
Lochran stays on the line, focused on whether the chamber has stabilized rather than on why engineering closed the path.
End on the technician holding the undeployed package over a clear conflict warning.
directionInline: The technician should clearly understand there is risk.

dialogueInline.text: Chair Davitt, your emergency key just reopened a local lockout.
Barely. Your package conflicts with the active matrix.

summary: Lochran orders the override executed anyway because the operation must produce reassuring metrics, and the technician obeys.
panelPlan: Lochran appears over the command channel demanding execution.
The technician looks from the authorization to the contradictory values.
A final warning prompt is acknowledged.
End on the override routing into the live damping cycle as console lights turn amber. Direction: The final panel must make the causal intrusion unmistakable.

dialogueInline.text: Your emergency key does not satisfy the engineering lockout.
Run the override under my authority.
Proceed. I will own the decision.

summary: Inside the chamber, a new surge enters a configuration Liora and Alan did not authorize.
panelPlan: Hard cut inside the Damping Chamber: the previously regular pulse develops a second rhythm underneath it.
Liora sees control values change without her input.
One emitter fires early and another compensates too late.
End on Liora recognizing that the live configuration is no longer theirs.
directionInline: Show the exact moment external control breaks the local calibration.

summary: Alan traces the surge to newly pushed coefficients that do not match the damping matrix.
panelPlan: Alan pulls the remote-change history while the chamber begins to shake.
The new coefficient set is highlighted against the calibrated matrix.
He identifies the mismatch as the source of the divergence.
A stronger pulse hits before they can roll it back.
directionInline: Keep the causal chain clear: override, mismatch, instability.

summary: The corrupted cycle turns violent, throwing Alan into a railing as emitters fall out of sequence.
panelPlan: Alarm insert: one emitter fires early.
Alan turns toward the feed as a second emitter answers out of sequence.
A violent field pulse throws Alan into the railing.
Liora catches the console rather than Alan because the cycle is already feeding itself.
Alan, hurt but conscious, drags herself back toward the manual controls.
Final narrow panel: the emitter pattern cascades red across the chamber.
directionInline: This is the physical point of no return for the experiment.

summary: Liora chooses shutdown over salvage and slams the manual abort before the feedback can grow further.
panelPlan: Liora sees one brief path back toward alignment while Alan starts calling the emitters she might recover.
Tight two-shot as Liora refuses the salvage attempt and reaches for the manual abort.
Large final panel: the chamber slams dark under emergency shutdown while residual harmonic light continues racing outward beyond it.
directionInline: The shutdown stops the machine but does not undo what the corrupted pulse already released into the network.

dialogueInline.text: If I can get four back in phase—
Then we lose it. If we keep chasing this, we make it worse.

summary: A ship in transit reports its own silhouette trailing behind it in open space after the failed damping cycle.
panelPlan: Open outside the ship with warped starlight and a delayed duplicate outline following the hull.
Inside, the captain watches a second version of the ship appear on sensors where nothing should be.
Crew members compare viewport and instrument readings and see the same impossible effect.
End on the captain calling the anomaly in.
directionInline: Make the duplicate clearly temporal or harmonic, not a second physical ship.

dialogueInline.text: Control, I have my own ship off our port quarter.
Same hull. Same running lights. Half a second behind us.

summary: Liora receives the transmission and identifies the doubling as harmonic folding rather than an optical error or superstition.
panelPlan: Liora listens from a damaged chamber console while the captain’s distorted feed plays beside network data.
She matches the delayed silhouette to the post-shutdown harmonic residue.
The duplicate ship image flickers closer to the real hull on the feed.
End on Liora naming the effect and understanding its scale.
directionInline: Her explanation should reduce mystery while increasing danger.

dialogueInline.text: It's a delayed harmonic image, not an optical reflection. Keep your engines cold; I need the separation to stay measurable.

summary: More corridor traces begin slipping their anchors, proving the failed intervention has propagated beyond the damping chamber.
panelPlan: Several route feeds populate beside the captain’s report with similar phase offsets.
A stable anchor marker drifts relative to its corridor path.
Liora watches the anomaly spread across more than one arc.
End on the network map showing the first visible tearing pattern.
directionInline: No new dialogue; let propagation carry the beat.

dialogueInline.text: Other routes are lighting up. Tell me this is local.

summary: Lochran tries to hold to containment as alarms begin sounding across multiple worlds and Council aides abandon normal procedure.
panelPlan: Establish Cooperative corridors in disorder: aides running, alarms crossing over public announcements.
Lochran insists that the event can still be contained while trying to maintain command posture.
Incident displays behind him add world after world.
End on his repeated claim visibly contradicted by the environment.
directionInline: This is the collapse of Lochran’s old operating assumption, not yet of the network itself.

dialogueInline.text: One channel. One set of instructions.
There isn't one situation anymore. Local channels are already giving different guidance.
Then make the message broad enough. People are asking who's in charge.

summary: Damian breaks with the reassurance strategy and says the public deserves the truth.
panelPlan: Damian looks from the emergency boards to the prepared reassurance language still open on a nearby display.
He closes or discards the old messaging draft.
Facing Lochran directly, he says the alarms now outrun their narrative.
End on Lochran realizing he has lost Damian’s support for containment messaging.
directionInline: Mark Damian’s turn through action as well as dialogue.

dialogueInline.text: The failures are no longer contained.
Then at least they know what they're running from.

summary: Iskara declares prevention over and orders preparation for coordinated failure, ending the issue on the shift from control to triage.
panelPlan: Council-wide panel under overlapping alarms: Lochran still faces the central command display while Iskara physically turns toward local rescue maps.
Damian joins Iskara at the triage table, leaving Lochran with the collapsing unified feed.
Final panel on Iskara's local-authority orders propagating outward as the old central display fragments behind them.

dialogueInline.text: Triage map. Local authority. Rescue priority.
Look around. It's already coming apart. I want people alive when it does.

summary: A corridor ship acquires a delayed duplicate as beacon anchors and route geometry begin to disagree with each other.
settingText: Full-page deep-space corridor image: a ship traveling inside a once-clean route has a faint delayed duplicate silhouette displaced beside it, while beacon anchors and luminous lane geometry show visible misalignment. The effect is physical, measurable, and increasingly dangerous.
panelPlan: Single full-page story-world splash. Use one cinematic full-bleed illustration rather than conventional story panels.
Build the beat entirely through environment, infrastructure, equipment, and human activity. No reserved text area and no readable copy.
directionInline: No captions or speech balloons.
No environmental lettering, labels, signage, logos, or incidental readable text.
Preserve the established historical period, faction precursor design, technology state, and accumulated damage for this point in continuity.
Use the visible situation itself to carry the beat.
